newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER - DUBOVSKY OUT AS SLOVAKS FACE FIRST BIG TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - DUBOVSKY OUT AS SLOVAKS FACE FIRST BIG TEST.

text.p: Six of the Barcelona and Atletico Madrid players who fought out an exhausting 3-3 classic at the weekend will form the backbone of Spain's team in Wednesday's vital World Cup qualifier against Slovakia.

But it is not just Javier Clemente's side who have been affected by Spanish league action, as influential Slovak striker Peter Dubovsky was injured while playing for Oviedo and will miss the European group six game.
"I believe the loss of Dubovsky is important for them. I hope they're affected," said Clemente.
Also out is Slovak captain Lubor Moravcik, who suffered a serious ankle injury in a French league game for Bastia, and is unlikely to reappear until the New Year.
Although Clemente and the Spanish players do not see Slovakia as the big threat in the group, they are convinced that a draw will not be enough after Yugoslavia's 1-0 win over the Czech Republic.
"We have to win against Slovakia, and hope to see them take points from some of the others," said Clemente.
Clemente's opposite number, Slovak coach Jozef Jankech, says he is undaunted by the fact that Spain will start the game as strong favourites.

"We are all well aware of the fact that Spain will go into the match with the only aim being to win, but we are not scared," said Jankech. "We believe that we are able to defend our position in the group."
For Slovakia, it will be the first big test of the World Cup qualifying campaign after three straightforward victories, two over the Faroe Islands and one over Malta.
Spain also won in the Faroe Islands, and secured a valuable point in Prague against the Czech Republic.
The Spanish contingent is free of injury problems, as energetic utility man Luis Enrique Martinez has recovered rapidly from a knock on his knee.
Both Luis Enrique and Barcelona colleague Josep Guardiola are likely to start after putting in exceptional performances against Atletico on Saturday.
Athletic Bilbao midfielder Julen Guerrero has also re-emerged as a probable starter, despite seeing his four-game league goal run broken in the 2-0 win over Valencia on Saturday.

Veteran goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta broke his own run of fine performances in that game with several of the elementary mistakes for which he has become infamous among Spanish fans. But 'Zubi', who is a favourite of fellow Basque Clemente, is almost certain to extend his record of Spanish caps to 113.
Spain - Andoni Zubizarreta, Alberto Belsue, Rafael Alkorta, Sergi Barjuan, Abelardo Fernandez, Fernando Hierro, Josep Guardiola, Luis Enrique Martinez, Julen Guerrero, Kiko Naraez, Alfonso Perez.
Slovakia - Alexander Vencel, Marian Zeman, Miroslav Karhan, Robert Tomaschek, Vladimir Kinder, Dusan Tittel, Samuel Slovak, Julius Simon, Jaroslav Timko, Marek Uljaky, Tibor Jancula.
